What the SBIR readings mean for people like me

Quick readMore contextTechnical detailSpeaker notes

The supplied SBIR handout presents competing views on stable support, commercialization, graduation, and opportunities for newcomers. A useful question across those views is: what did continued support change?

  • Cohen, Feldman and Stern: SBIR is mission infrastructure; success looks different across agencies; use many measures and better integrated data.
  • Schönander: reauthorization is not enough; open the door to first-time applicants; assess commercialization readiness explicitly; try lotteries and golden tickets for ideas consensus review misses.
  • Katz: seed funding should graduate firms; weight commercial viability heavily; provide procurement pathways.
  • The Murphy interview: ask what past awards produced; share past-performance and technical learning across agencies.

Common thread: reward demonstrable progress and learning. That needs records richer than pass or fail.

These are summaries of discussion positions in the handout, not current eligibility rules or funding decisions.

Participant proposals for the Widener-led, NSF-funded convening. Project examples include documented results, work in development, and proposed pilots.
